causal.assumptions_right: The bill, not the currency, was the right place to test the Australia path, and leaving once the strip stepped down kept the miss small.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A contract already above cash was treated as a hike still to come. The chance that the strip would step down from the front was underweighted.
causal.causal_divergence: The pay needed a higher implied rate. The strip stepped down instead, so the hike-cycle thesis was not what the bills delivered.
causal.future_implication: The next Australian bill pay has to be a contract that is actually on a hike path. That is why the September Australia pay is closed today.
causal.observed_reality: The pay was closed on 13 November after the Australian strip stepped down and the contract was marked lower.
causal.original_belief: June 2027 Australia bills were only a modest step above cash, so an underpriced hiking cycle would lift the contract.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same strip, the June pay would have been closed once contracts were stepping down from the front, rather than held as a hawkish identity trade.

facts.invalidation: The view breaks if the US 10-year reverses away from the 2002 high together with a break in oil while Sep-27 SOFR and Jun-27 AONIA stop repricing higher, or if Jun-27 AONIA trades up through the AU 10-year at 5.245 and the cash-to-contract gap is closed.

items.future_rule: Keep an Australian bill pay only while that contract is on a hike path above cash. A strip that is flat in front and lower in the back is an exit.
items.lesson: An Australian bill pay is not an underpriced hiking cycle once the strip is flat at the front and lower in the back.
items.thesis_assessment: A contract already above the then cash rate was treated as a hike that still had to be priced. The later strip was flat to lower.
items.what_failed: The June 2027 Australia pay failed as an underpriced hiking cycle. The strip stepped down instead of extending.

causal.assumptions_right: The bill was the right instrument, and the next-day exit recognized that the back of the strip was ease rather than a fresh hike.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Opening a contract already below cash treated a hawkish bias as a reason to pay a cut the strip was still pricing.
causal.causal_divergence: The intended mark was a rise toward the cash anchor. One session later the contract had not risen and the position was closed.
causal.future_implication: Do not keep a short that is the easy side of cash. The same exit rule closes the remaining September Australia pay.
causal.observed_reality: The pay was closed one day later with the strip still pricing a contract under cash near 4.85.
causal.original_belief: December 2027 Australia bills under the cash rate would be taken out, so the priced ease was a pay.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same strip the December pay would not have been opened. If it had been opened, the next-day cover would still have been the action.

facts.invalidation: The new pay is wrong if December 2027 AONIA falls further below 4.65 while the front of the Australian strip drops back and the US December step is marked back toward an unchanged path.

items.no_new_lesson: The small loss one day after entry is bounded variance inside the risk budget. The original process remains sound because the pay was closed the next session once the strip still priced ease rather than a hike.
items.thesis_assessment: The ease-fade was not confirmed. Closing it the next session kept the miss small instead of turning a below-cash pay into a campaign.
items.what_failed: The December 2027 Australia pay was opened on the easy side of cash and did not rise toward the cash anchor in the one session it was held.

causal.assumptions_right: The September contract was cheap to cash and the implied rate did rise from about 4.71 to 4.815, so the narrow mechanism that a priced cut would be reduced operated in the direction of the pay.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The entry equated removal of one cut with a hiking cycle that would take September through cash, but the RBA can set a higher near-term rate and still ease by late 2027, which is the path March at 4.92 versus September at 4.815 was already describing.
causal.causal_divergence: The level moved in favor of the pay because part of the embedded cut came out, but the mechanism required to finish the move through cash was a path with no residual easing, and the strip delivered a higher March fixing while September remained below both March and cash.
causal.future_implication: A new September AONIA pay is warranted only if September implied trades above cash and the March-September spread stops pricing later cuts. Until then the hawkish Australian information sits in the front of the strip.
causal.observed_reality: The pay was opened on 10 November and closed on 16 November, and the fresh September 2027 settlement is 4.815, higher than the entry area but still short of cash, while March 2027 AONIA at 4.92 is already above that cash rate.
causal.original_belief: September 2027 AONIA near 4.71 embedded an RBA cut versus cash near 4.85, so paying that contract would work as the cut was removed and the implied rate was pulled back through the cash rate.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry information the position should have been a cut-removal pay with a curve-shape exit: once March was above cash and September was still below cash, the back-contract pay should have been closed rather than held for a print through cash.

facts.invalidation: The Australia pay is wrong if inflation cools and September AONIA stays below cash, or if the RBA validates cuts inside the next two meetings. The SOFR cut is wrong if September 2027 SOFR reprices sustainably above 4.60.

items.future_rule: Exit a back-contract policy pay when the preceding contract is already above cash and the back contract remains below cash, because that curve is residual easing and not an unfinished hike.
items.lesson: Removing one priced cut and starting a hiking cycle are different policy paths, and the March-versus-September AONIA spread is the market's statement of which path is priced.
items.thesis_assessment: The pay correctly identified a cut that was too large in September 2027 AONIA, and implied rose from about 4.71 to a 4.815 settlement, but it wrongly treated that removal as a hiking cycle that would carry the contract through cash near 4.85.
items.what_failed: The claim that deleting one priced cut would reprice September as the hiking-cycle contract failed, because the strip lifted March 2027 to 4.92 and left September at 4.815, still under cash.

causal.assumptions_right: A true hiking cycle, as distinct from removing one cut, was the only path that could pay the short.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The oil pair used as the invalidation did not describe the oil market that traded, and there was no exit tied to the Canada path itself.
causal.causal_divergence: Brent could stay near 93 while the forward moved toward easier policy, so the oil premise and the rate path diverged.
causal.future_implication: Do not re-short Canada March at 2.965 to replay the 3.12 entry, and do not replace it with an Australian bill pay on a strip that is flat at the front and lower in the back.
causal.observed_reality: The contract fell from 3.12 to 2.96, a loss, while oil is now 86 and 93 rather than 105. The later print at 2.965 did not rebuild a hiking cycle.
causal.original_belief: A short Canada March future at 3.12 would pay if firmer oil forced a hiking cycle rather than merely removing one priced cut.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: An exit when the Canada forward itself fell, rather than when oil revisited 105, would have recognized that the hiking cycle was not being delivered.

items.expression_assessment: The invalidation lived in the oil market rather than in the forward being shorted. Brent near 93 could not keep the short right once the contract had dropped and there was no rule that closed it when the Canada path itself eased.

facts.invalidation: Iran-deal pessimism lifts and Brent/WTI reverse sharply from 105.28/92.60, letting BoC stay near 2.30 and sending U7 back through 4.75; or a yen-warning risk-off duration bid that cheapens pays without a hawkish policy rethink.

items.future_rule: Invalidate a short-rate position on that contract's own path. If the forward falls and the strip is not pricing hikes, the hiking-cycle thesis is finished even when Brent is still in the low 90s. Do not pay Australian bills when the front is 5.00 and the back is 4.88.
items.lesson: The position was the Canada forward, and that forward fell from 3.12 to 2.96. Oil near 105 was a stale premise and left the hawkish rethink without a rate path.
items.thesis_assessment: The thesis treated firmer oil as the opening of a Canadian hiking cycle. From 3.12 to 2.96 the forward added easing. Shedding one priced cut and starting a hiking cycle are different paths, and this short was paid only by the second.
items.what_failed: The Canada March short from 3.12 to 2.96 lost 16bp. The invalidation named oil near 105 and 93 and a hawkish rethink. Oil is now 86 and 93, so the 105 premise was stale, and the contract fell anyway.

causal.assumptions_right: December hike pricing was too low, because implied rose from 4.12 to 4.30. The jobs and oil breaks did not arrive, so the short was not run over by an easing narrative.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The exit rule underweighted how completely a front contract can finish its repricing once the strip has climbed from 3.92 toward the mid-4s. It also underweighted that the two-year rose while September fell from 4.755 to 4.735.
causal.causal_divergence: The trade did not end on its stated invalidation. December moved because the policy path was marked toward more hikes, and the cover landed on a contract that has since sat near 4.30.
causal.future_implication: Harvest the front short when that contract has priced the path and fresh hawkish talk is being marked into the two-year. Keep the peak contract as a separate decision.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed at 4.29 and December is now 4.30. There is no weak jobs report in the marks, and Brent at 91.95 with WTI at 83.26 is not oil breaking lower.
causal.original_belief: December 2026 secured funding at 4.12 underpriced further hikes. The short was to be dropped if a weak jobs report opened the door to easing or if oil broke lower.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry, the same jobs-or-oil invalidation, and the same path to 4.29, the short was the position to hold through that repricing. The marks do not show a second leg after the exit.

facts.invalidation: The shorts are invalidated if the jobs report is weak enough to extend the rally and policy treats that weakness as room to ease, or if oil breaks lower and removes the inflation impulse.

items.future_rule: Cover a front secured-funding short when that contract has built the path and fresh hawkish communication is showing up in the two-year rather than in the contract. Do not roll the closed front short into the peak contract to keep the thesis alive.
items.lesson: A short-rate short is finished when the contract that had room to price incremental hikes has built that path. A peak contract does not inherit the result just because the reaction function is still described as hawkish.
items.thesis_assessment: The hawkish front-end thesis was confirmed. December rose from 4.12 into the 4.29 area and then stalled. The thesis was not invalidated. It reached the front contract and stopped.
items.what_failed: The written invalidation was a weak jobs report or oil breaking lower, and neither caused the outcome. The exit rule did not say what to do when the front contract finished the hike repricing with oil still firm.
items.what_worked: The December 2026 secured-funding short was the contract that actually repriced, from 4.12 to a cover at 4.29. December is now 4.30, and the jobs and oil invalidation never became the exit.
